title: A Complete Shell Test Harness
description: test_runner.sh loops over every test program, compares the interpreter's output to its expected file, and counts passes and failures.

steps.description: The first line is the shebang. `PASS=0; FAIL=0` starts two counters. The shell expands the glob `tests/*.ml` into the list of matching file paths before the loop starts, and each iteration assigns one path to the variable `test`.

`name=$(basename "$test" .ml)` runs `basename` in a subshell and captures its output, stripping the directory prefix and the `.ml` suffix. `expected` builds the matching expected file path. `actual=$(python3 mylang.py "$test" 2>&1)` runs the interpreter and captures both stdout and stderr.
The condition checks that the expected file exists and that `diff -q` finds the two files identical. `-q` is quiet mode, so it prints nothing. A match prints `PASS` and increments the pass counter.
The else branch prints `FAIL`. When an expected file exists, `diff` prints the differences. Either way the failure counter increments.
The loop ends and the script prints the results. `[ $FAIL -eq 0 ]` is the last command, so its exit code becomes the script's exit code: 0 when all tests pass, 1 when any test fails.
